sections.overview: Montagu’s Harrier is a slender migratory raptor that breeds across much of Eurasia and spends the non-breeding season mainly in sub-Saharan Africa.
sections.identification: The male is grey with black wing markings, while the brown female and juvenile show a pale rump; it is smaller and more slender than many other harriers.
sections.habitat: It hunts over open grassland, heath, marsh edges and farmland, and often nests in cereal fields where natural tall vegetation is scarce.
sections.diet: Its flexible diet includes small mammals, birds, reptiles and large insects, with prey varying by place and season.
sections.behavior: It quartering-flies low over open ground while hunting and makes long seasonal migrations between Eurasian breeding areas and African wintering grounds.
sections.reproduction: The species nests on the ground, often in crops; eggs and young can be lost when fields are harvested before fledging.
sections.ecology: It shares the open-country hunting style of other Circus harriers, including the Hen Harrier, but differs in its grey male and characteristic black wing bars.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern while noting a decreasing population; nest protection in farmland addresses an important local risk.
